title: Normalized derived coefficient transport along a ring-sheaf isomorphism
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $\alpha:R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ be an isomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings on it. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], cochain complexes, and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $T_\alpha=(\alpha^{-1})_*:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(S)$; on sections the $S$-action is $s\cdot m=\alpha^{-1}(s)m$ and on module morphisms its underlying map is unchanged.

There is an additive exact equivalence $T_\alpha$, with inverse $\alpha_*$, and a triangulated derived equivalence $D(T_\alpha):D(R)\simeq D(S)$ with a specified natural isomorphism
$$Q_R\,D(T_\alpha)\cong\operatorname{Ch}(T_\alpha)\,Q_S.$$
Here juxtaposition denotes functors in their order of application, $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms, and $\operatorname{Ch}$ is termwise application. The displayed isomorphism also identifies the maps of localized chain maps and roofs. For $R\xrightarrow{\alpha}S\xrightarrow{\beta}T$, the composition comparison $D(T_\beta)D(T_\alpha)\cong D(T_{\beta\alpha})$ (composition here in the usual right-to-left order) is the descent of the identity on underlying abelian complexes and satisfies the identity and three-isomorphism cocycle.

Use sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex], and the K-flat derived tensor of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Transport preserves flat modules and K-flat complexes. There are natural comparisons
$$T_\alpha M\otimes_S T_\alpha N\cong T_\alpha(M\otimes_RN),\qquad T_\alpha R\cong S,$$
with maps $m\otimes n\mapsto m\otimes n$ and $r\mapsto\alpha(r)$. They descend to derived tensor products and identify associators, symmetry, units, and the preceding composition comparisons. No boundedness or constructibility is assumed.

proof.text: Choose simultaneous symmetric tensor localizations whose tensor bifunctors are literally the published K-flat tensor, by [lem-pur-u2-published-derived-tensor]. This constructs actual monoidal data by transport of the native tensor and uses rigidity only for its determined comparison.

For each ring isomorphism choose the existing normalized ordinary inverse-restriction transport from [lem-sfb-ring-isomorphism-tensor-transport]. The exact derived functor is an equivalence by Mathlib. For the chosen tensor localizations, [lem-pur-u2-normalized-braided-derived] gives the normalized braided derived structure and monoidality of the canonical factorization.

Use the identity-on-sections chain comparisons and exact derived unit/compositor of [lem-pur-u2-restriction-comparisons]. Their component formulas are precisely the required localization and chain specifications.

The source exact-derived compositor unit and cocycle laws specialize to inverse coefficient restriction by [lem-pur-u2-derived-restriction-cocycle]. The ordinary comparisons are identity on sections, and the displayed reassociation is identity.

The ordinary pure-tensor and unit equations lift to total cochain complexes, and normalized factorization pastings descend their monoidality to all derived objects by [lem-pur-u2-derived-restriction-monoidal]. K-flat models and invertibility of localization tensorators give reflection of the tensor equation. Assemble the data and six named specifications without changing their statements.
